title: How Wrong a Pose Is: Position Error, Orientation Error as a Rotation Vector, and Why Euler Angles Cannot Be Subtracted

questions.question: A yaw of 359 degrees and one of -1 degree. What is the difference of the Euler angles, and the rotation error?
options: -360 degrees, and a rotation error of nearly 0
questions.explanation: They are the same orientation. The rotation error was 9.4e-16 rad.

questions.question: What is the rotation vector?
options: The axis of the turn from one orientation to the other, times its angle
questions.explanation: It is zero for the same orientation.

questions.question: Why does the arc cosine of the trace fail for a turn of 1e-10?
questions.explanation: The angle is 0 and the answer is lost. The antisymmetric part gave 1e-10.

questions.question: Where is the axis of a half turn?
questions.explanation: The antisymmetric part is zero there. R is 2 k kT less I at a half turn.

questions.question: A pose is right in position and 0.1 rad out in orientation. Is it converged?
options: No: it needs both to be within their tolerances
questions.explanation: The position error was 0 m and the rotation error 0.1 rad.

questions.question: What does swapping the order of target and transpose of current do to the vector?
options: It gives the turn the other way, with the opposite sign
questions.explanation: The error one way is minus the error the other.
